Score a word by summing the Scrabble values of its letters.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/scrabble-score) (MIT). Listed under [Strings & Text](/examples/?subject=strings-and-text).

```nomi-run
// FILE: scrabble_score.nomi
//# A word's Scrabble score.

/// The sum of the letter values in `word`, in either case. Anything that is
/// not a Latin letter scores nothing.
pub fn score(word: String) -> Int {
    word
    |> String.fold_case()
    |> Iter.map(letter_value)
    |> Iter.sum()
}

fn letter_value(letter: String) -> Int {
    case letter {
        "a" or "e" or "i" or "o" or "u" or "l" or "n" or "r" or "s" or "t" -> 1
        "d" or "g" -> 2
        "b" or "c" or "m" or "p" -> 3
        "f" or "h" or "v" or "w" or "y" -> 4
        "k" -> 5
        "j" or "x" -> 8
        "q" or "z" -> 10
        _ -> 0
    }
}

// FILE: scrabble_score_test.nomi
import scrabble_score

test "score" {
    cases = [
        #("lowercase letter", "a", 1),
        #("uppercase letter", "A", 1),
        #("valuable letter", "f", 4),
        #("short word", "at", 2),
        #("short, valuable word", "zoo", 12),
        #("medium word", "street", 6),
        #("medium, valuable word", "quirky", 22),
        #("long, mixed-case word", "OxyphenButazone", 41),
        #("english-like word", "pinata", 8),
        #("empty input", "", 0),
        #("entire alphabet available", "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz", 87),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, word, expected), description {
        assert scrabble_score.score(word) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- The letter table is one `case` over one-letter strings, each value one arm with its letters joined by `or` (style §25). A `Map` built from the table was the other option; the `case` reads as the problem's table and needs no lookup that may miss.
- The word is case-folded once with `String.fold_case`, then iterated as graphemes, so the table lists lowercase letters only.
- The total is `Iter.sum` (style §26).
- Anything not in the table scores 0, which the canonical data does not test.
